theme: Big Tech capex misses hit the neoclouds and Alphabet, the 10-year tops 5%, Tesla's Cybercabs take over its Texas fleet, and Strategy reports after a quiet week for bitcoin.

items.title: Texas robotaxi registrations: Tesla vs Waymo, Avride and Zoox
items.picked: Cybercabs now make up the majority of Tesla's Texas robotaxi registrations, and Tesla shares hit a three-month high on Oct 27 as the fleet passed 1,000. Tesla also widened its Houston service area to about 254 square miles this week.
items.matters: Tesla is closing in on Waymo in Waymo's second-biggest state, and nearly all of its recent additions are the no-steering-wheel Cybercab rather than Model Ys.
items.know: As of Oct 28 the tab has Tesla at 1,080 registered vehicles (573 Cybercabs, 507 Model Ys) against Waymo at 1,207, a gap of 127, with Avride at 344 and Zoox at 63. Waymo's count is from its Oct 19 registry update and Avride and Zoox haven't changed since Oct 11. These are registrations, not cars carrying riders, and this image was redrawn from the sheet because the Drive export was from Oct 19.

items.title: Waymo paid rides per week, May 2023 to Mar 2026
items.picked: A chart going viral this morning puts Tesla's Austin robotaxis at 438K miles a week against Waymo's 406K. This chart shows the scale Waymo has reached across all its cities.
items.matters: Waymo's network-wide ride count is the benchmark Tesla has to beat, and it's a useful reality check on single-city comparisons.
items.know: Waymo went from 10,000 paid rides a week in May 2023 to 450,000 in Dec 2025 and 500,000 in Mar 2026, and TechCrunch still reported about 500,000 on Sep 24. Waymo's target is 1 million a week by the end of 2026. The milestones fall on irregular dates and count rides, not miles, so they can't be compared directly with the viral Austin miles chart.

items.title: Strategy's USD Reserve vs its yearly preferred dividends and interest
items.picked: Strategy reports Q3 results today at 5pm ET, a day after shareholders approved daily dividends on STRF, STRC, STRK and STRD with 99.3% in favor, starting with STRC on Nov 1. Last week it bought no bitcoin and spent about $205M buying back STRC.
items.matters: The cash reserve is what lets Strategy pay its preferred dividends without selling bitcoin or new stock, and it's the cushion behind the buybacks.
items.know: On Oct 16 the tab has the USD Reserve at $4,878M against $1,557M of yearly preferred dividends and interest, enough for 37.6 months. The low point was 6.1 months on May 29 2026. The tab ends Oct 16, so it misses the $205M STRC buyback and the $4.83B reserve Strategy reported on Oct 26.

items.title: Bitcoin options: implied volatility (Deribit DVOL) vs 30-day realized volatility
items.picked: Glassnode data trending on X shows bitcoin's one-month realized volatility near 25%, the quietest since mid-2023, with the price stuck around $80,000-81,000 after the Fed held rates. This chart shows how options traders are pricing that calm.
items.matters: Long stretches of low volatility often come before a big move, and the gap between implied and realized vol shows whether options are cheap or expensive.
items.know: On Oct 16 the tab has DVOL implied vol at 37.66% and 30-day realized vol at 36.77%, a gap of +0.89 points, after implied ran below realized every week from Aug 21 to Oct 9. Realized vol peaked at 46.57% on Sep 11. The weekly data ends Oct 16, and Glassnode's ~25% reading is a later, different measure that isn't in the tab.

items.title: SpaceX after the IPO: drawdown from record close and 10-day volatility vs Tesla
items.picked: SPCX fell 2.25% to $145.23 on Oct 28, back near the $140 level Yahoo Finance calls support, a week after an unlock of up to 1.3 billion shares sent it down 9.14% on Oct 22. A lawsuit over its Louisiana spaceport tax deal added pressure, while Fitch affirmed its BBB+ rating after the roughly $40B Nvidia GPU lease.
items.matters: The drawdown shows how far SPCX still sits below its June peak, and the volatility lines show it still trades far more wildly than Tesla.
items.know: On Oct 20 SPCX was 30.09% below its record close, with 10-day volatility of 33.75% vs 30.84% for Tesla. Its deepest drawdown was 48.78% on Aug 5 and its shallowest recent one was 18.67% on Oct 6. The data ends Oct 20, so the Oct 22 unlock drop isn't in it.

items.title: Quarterly capex at Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta and Oracle
items.picked: Microsoft's capex of $45.2B (including finance leases) missed the $50.7B estimate and it trimmed its 2026 plan to about $170B from $175B, citing delayed third-party capacity. Alphabet's $51.36B also came in below the $55.09B expected, though it kept its $195-205B guide.
items.matters: The capex race is the demand engine for Nvidia, the neoclouds and the power trade, so even a timing miss moves all of them.
items.know: In the Jun 2026 quarter the tab has Amazon at $54.21B, Alphabet $44.92B, Microsoft $35.80B, Meta $30.12B and Oracle $16.49B, $181.5B combined vs $97.3B a year earlier. The tab ends with the Jun quarter, so this week's Sep-quarter numbers aren't in it yet. The tab's Microsoft numbers are cash capex without finance leases, so they run below headline figures like the $45.2B.

items.title: Alphabet: operating cash flow, capex and free cash flow per quarter
items.picked: Alphabet fell about 10% premarket after missing Q3 revenue and EPS estimates and reporting negative free cash flow of $9.07B, per CNBC. This chart shows how capex overtook cash from operations.
items.matters: Alphabet was one of the biggest cash machines in the market, so negative free cash flow is a big shift and feeds the worry that AI spending is outrunning returns.
items.know: In the Jun 2026 quarter the tab has operating cash flow of $39.07B, capex of $44.92B and free cash flow of -$5.86B, the only negative quarter since 2019, after $10.12B in Mar 2026 and $24.55B in Dec 2025. The tab ends with the Jun quarter, so the Q3 -$9.07B reported Wednesday isn't in it yet.

items.title: Neocloud debt as a % of market cap
items.picked: CoreWeave fell 5.8%, Nebius 6.3%, IREN 5.3% and Applied Digital 4.3% after hours on Microsoft's capex miss, since Microsoft relies on them for extra capacity. CNBC notes their cost of capital is rising as worries about their debt mount.
items.matters: These companies fund their buildouts with borrowing, so the debt load relative to equity value shows which ones are most exposed if lenders pull back or capacity slips.
items.know: Using Oct 21 closing prices, the tab has Cipher at 149.7% ($6.23B debt vs $4.16B market cap), CoreWeave at 115.8% ($39.49B vs $34.09B), Applied Digital 101.2%, TeraWulf 81.8%, IREN 71.5% and Nebius 27.3%. Operating leases (CoreWeave's $16.3B) and undrawn facilities are left out, and share prices have moved since Oct 21.

items.title: Cost to insure AI borrowers' debt: 5-year CDS spreads
items.picked: Posts trending on X say at least 18 data center deals now carry double-digit yields and default insurance is at records for Oracle, Meta and SpaceX. Oracle still jumped 10.73% Wednesday on a $225B fiscal 2030 revenue target.
items.matters: CDS spreads are the bond market's live read on credit risk, and they show which AI spenders lenders worry about most.
items.know: The tab has Oracle at 261 bps (Oct 9), SpaceX 197 (Oct 7), Broadcom 136 (Oct 9), Meta 95, Nvidia 89, Amazon 73, Alphabet 72 and Microsoft 52 (all Sep 28), against 55 for the CDX IG index. These levels are quoted from X posts because CDS data is paywalled, the dates differ, it isn't a time series, and any move since early October isn't shown.

items.title: 10-year term premium (ACM model) vs the 10-year Treasury yield
items.picked: The 10-year Treasury yield closed above 5% on Wednesday at 5.044%, up 5.2 bps, after the Fed held at 3.75-4.00% with two officials preferring a hike. Brent also settled at $115.32.
items.matters: A rising term premium means investors want extra pay to hold long bonds, which pushes up mortgage rates and the borrowing costs of AI builders.
items.know: On Sep 25 2026 the tab has the term premium at 1.02% and the 10-year at 5.17%, the first reading at or above 1% since Apr 2010; it was 0.70% in Jun 2026 and 0.57% in Dec 2025. The data is month-end except that last Sep 25 point, so October is missing, and the ACM premium is a model estimate.
